abstract: Background and Aims: APOBEC-associated mutagenesis is prominent in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), but genomic features associated with its intertumoral variability remain incompletely characterized. We investigated genomic correlates of APOBEC-associated mutagenesis while accounting for the compositional structure of mutational signature data. Methods: Mutational signatures were analyzed in 552 ESCC tumors from eight countries. APOBEC-associated mutagenesis was quantified as SBS2 plus SBS13 using absolute mutation counts and proportional contributions. Associations with co-occurring mutational signatures, total SBS burden, recurrent driver-gene alterations, and country were evaluated using correlation, sensitivity, and multivariable analyses. Principal component and regression-model robustness were additionally assessed. Results: APOBEC burden varied markedly across tumors (median, 2,002 mutations; IQR, 987-4,346). Several associations observed using signature proportions were not maintained in absolute-count analyses: SBS1, SBS3, and SBS5 changed direction, indicating sensitivity to compositional representation. In contrast, SBS18 remained inversely associated with APOBEC-associated mutagenesis in all variable pairings examined: proportion versus proportion (Spearman rho = -0.527), APOBEC proportion versus SBS18 absolute count (r = -0.435), and absolute count versus absolute count (Pearson r = -0.319, P = 1.59 x 10^-14; Spearman rho = -0.317). These are distinct comparisons rather than discrepant estimates. Notably, this cohort-wide relationship was primarily characterized by higher APOBEC burden in SBS18-negative than SBS18-positive tumors rather than a continuous inverse relationship among SBS18-positive tumors. The multivariable model had an in-sample R^2 of 0.400 but lower and variable 10-fold cross-validated performance (mean R^2 = 0.273). Country added little explanatory information to this model (delta R^2 = 0.008; global P = 0.402). ZNF750-mutant tumors had higher APOBEC burden than wild-type tumors (BH-FDR q = 0.0032), although only 12 tumors carried ZNF750 alterations. Conclusion: Genomic correlates of APOBEC-associated mutagenesis in ESCC are sensitive to the representation of mutational signature activity. SBS18 showed the most consistent inverse association, whereas the ZNF750 association warrants independent validation.
